title: Density-operator inductive bias on neurOS and EEG representations
objective: Determine what, if anything, density-operator normalization or downstream operator structure contributes after first proving that the current density constructor is information-equivalent to a trace-normalized Hermitian second moment and then comparing against strong classical geometry on identical neurOS/foundation representations and frozen longitudinal evidence authority.
decision_gates: Primary longitudinal lanes must consume merged neurOS LongitudinalCaseAuthority / GroupedEvaluationData evidence and may not silently re-split samples or alter the fixed final evaluation set across calibration budgets.
No subject/session leakage is permitted; target calibration examples must remain disjoint from final evaluation and future sessions must remain outside historical source training.

Scientific identity must bind upstream/raw-data authority, neurOS processed-data SHA, authority/partition/calibration fingerprints, exact representation SHA, QuantumBCI source revision, and neurOS source revision.

The current density constructor rho = X^H X / Tr(X^H X) is information-equivalent to a trace-normalized Hermitian second moment. An exact normalized-covariance control is mandatory and representation-information novelty is automatically ineligible while that equivalence holds.

Promotion-oriented comparisons must include normalized covariance, ordinary covariance, log-covariance geometry, bilinear second moment, pooled features, train-only PCA, diagonal density, and the fixed-readout off-diagonal intervention on identical token tensors.

Any predictive difference against weaker controls must be attributed to normalization/readout parameterization or inductive bias, not additional quantum information, unless a separately specified non-equivalent mechanism passes its own mathematical audit.
Off-diagonal removal measures dependence on cross-feature covariance structure. It must not be described as evidence for microscopic quantum coherence.

Statistical inference must resample participants (or the declared independent deployment unit), first aggregating repeated held-out sessions within participant; window/trial bootstrap is not a valid promotion test.
A negative equivalence or matched-control result is a successful scientific run and should block downstream novelty claims rather than be treated as infrastructure failure.
